name: All in One SEO
summary: WordPress SEO plugin for titles, schema, sitemaps and redirects.
best_for: WordPress site owners and agencies who want titles, schema, sitemaps and redirects in one plugin and accept yearly licences
skip_if: your site is not on WordPress, you want a free plugin version on this page, or you want a tool we have tested end to end
honest_knock: The first-year price is half the regular price and every renewal is at full price. The pricing page stated USD but showed euro amounts when we read it. Renewals are non-refundable.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-14 on aioseo.com/pricing) All in One SEO sells four yearly plans. Basic covers 1 site with 10,000 AI credits and lists smart schema markup, WooCommerce SEO and XML sitemaps; it is shown at 49.50 for the first year and regular at 99. Plus covers 3 sites with 25,000 AI credits and adds local SEO; shown at 99.50, regular 199. Pro covers 10 sites with 50,000 AI credits and adds the internal link assistant and advanced redirects; shown at 199.50, regular 399. Elite covers 100 sites with 200,000 AI credits and adds keyword rank tracking and client management; shown at 299.50, regular 599. The page says all pricing is in USD but displayed euro amounts when we read it, so confirm the currency at checkout. All renewals are at full price. There is a 14-day money-back guarantee, renewals are non-refundable, and AI credits are refundable within 14 days if fewer than 500 were used. The page mentions no free version of the plugin.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 in WordPress Playground, a temporary WordPress site that runs in the browser, with the free AIOSEO Lite plugin (version 5.0.5.1) from WordPress.org and the interface in English. We went through the seven step setup wizard, set a custom SEO title and meta description on a post with unique test codes, and checked the page head WordPress produced for that post. We paid nothing and opened the Basic checkout only to read the price.
findings: Setup: no AIOSEO account or licence key is needed for Lite. The last wizard step said you are using AIOSEO Lite and no licence is needed.

Extra installs: step 3 of the wizard had Broken Link Checker, MonsterInsights, OptinMonster and Universally ticked by default, plus the Pro addons Image SEO and Author SEO. We unticked each one, and afterwards only AIOSEO was installed.

Data sharing: step 4 had email reports set to Yes, and step 5 filled in the site admin email to connect the site to the AIOSEO SEO API with usage sharing switched on. We turned reports off and skipped step 5.

Titles and descriptions: the AIOSEO panel under the post editor updated its search preview as we typed. After saving, the page head carried our title, our meta description, a canonical link and matching Open Graph and Twitter titles.
Schema: without any setting from us, the post page carried BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList, Organization, Person, WebPage and WebSite markup.
Free and Pro: Search Console statistics, Link Assistant, Local SEO, Index Now and video and news sitemaps were marked Pro in the wizard. The general XML sitemap was switched on by default in Lite.

Checkout: on 22 November 2026, shown in euros from the Netherlands, Basic was €49.50 for the first year for one site (normally €99). The checkout added 21% VAT for a total of €59.90 and asked for an email, name and password for a new AIOSEO account. AIOSEO's terms say discount codes apply to the first term only. We did not pay.
not_tested: the paid plans and Pro features such as Search Console statistics, Link Assistant, Local SEO and video or news sitemaps
the XML sitemap output itself: the sandbox could not serve sitemap.xml, so we only saw that the sitemap was switched on
the AI Copilot, redirects and the SEO analysis scores
managing many client sites: we used one temporary site
the Basic checkout beyond reading the price; we did not pay
a live public site: the test ran in a temporary WordPress Playground site in our browser
